newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends down at two-month low against US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends down at two-month low against US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed down at an intraday low of 8.2964 on Tuesday, its lowest closing point in two months, after ending on Monday at 8.2958 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai, dealers said.
They said some speculative selling emerged late in the trading session, which depressed the local currency.
The weighted average price on Monday was 8.2958.
The yuan opened up at a high of 8.2860 and fell to consolidate around 8.2960 for most of the session. Trading was active.
"With a high trade surplus over the past two months, more selling emerged today to force the yuan down," said one dealer.
Official figures showed China's trade surplus for the first two months of 1997 was $3.8 billion.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to move around 8.2960 to the U.S. dollar on Wednesday.
The yuan closed slightly down at 6.7098 from 6.7003 against 100 Japanese yen and up at 1.0701 from 1.0719 against the Hong Kong dollar.
